title: Trump has left the US in ruins, but the repair work starts now
gist: Alan Rusbridger lays out a post-midterm repair agenda for the Democratic Congress, arguing that with a vetoing lame-duck president most legislative reversals (clean-energy credits, institutional rebuilding) must wait until 2029, while oversight, funding controls and corruption investigations can begin now; the cheapest damage to undo is symbolic, the costliest is lost expertise, trust and Supreme Court precedent.

themes.theme: Lame-duck constraints on the Democratic repair agenda

insights.claim: With the new Congress seated on 3 January, Rusbridger expects Trump as a lame-duck president to veto everything he can for the next two years, so Democrats should prepare restorative legislation ready for after he leaves.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Expect legislative gridlock through 2028; policy-reversal trades should be timed for 2029, not 2027.
insights.quote: For the next two years, we can expect the lame-duck occupant of the White House to veto everything he can.

insights.claim: Rusbridger's framework: the most visible, symbolic acts such as renamings are cheapest to undo, while the least visible damage (lost expertise, broken trust, deaths abroad, Supreme Court precedent) is the most expensive and slowest, and political energy risks flowing to the wrong places.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Headline reversals will come fast but structural repair (and its fiscal cost) will lag for years.
insights.quote: The most visible, symbolic acts (eg names) are the cheapest to undo, while the least visible (lost expertise, broken trust, deaths abroad, Supreme Court precedent) are the most expensive and the slowest.

insights.claim: Although Congress cannot easily remove officials such as FBI director Kash Patel, it controls funding levers and can impose enforceable restrictions, independent scrutiny, investigations and evidence-preservation orders.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Appropriations riders become the key battleground; watch budget fights and shutdown risk.
insights.locator: Congress can’t easily sack Kash Patel

insights.claim: The Supreme Court is likely to be 'preserved in aspic' for two years because Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito, in their mid-to-late seventies, have signalled they will not retire, leaving the power to rebalance the court to Trump's successor.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Court composition becomes a central 2028 election stake with long-run regulatory implications.

themes.theme: Clean-energy policy whiplash and the US risk premium

insights.claim: Restoring clean-energy tax credits requires a new law and a willing president, so realistically it will not happen before 2029; the Inflation Reduction Act's credits were originally estimated at around $370bn over a decade.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: US renewables developers face no federal credit tailwind until at least 2029; price in a policy-restoration option only post-2028 election.
insights.quote: Restoring clean energy credits would need a law and a president willing to sign it, so realistically it’s not going to happen before 2029.
insights.locator: It’s not going to be easy

insights.claim: The deeper cost of policy reversals is investor confidence: capital that has learned US clean-energy policy can flip every four years will demand a risk premium or go elsewhere.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Higher cost of capital for long-dated US clean-energy projects; relative advantage for jurisdictions with stable policy.
insights.quote: capital that has learned US clean-energy policy can flip every four years will demand a risk premium, or go elsewhere
insights.locator: It’s not going to be easy

insights.claim: Trump's war on offshore wind represents about $4bn in sunk cost, and new lease sales, permissions and construction can take the best part of a decade to restart.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: US offshore wind pipeline recovery is a decade-long story; near-term supply chain demand stays depressed.
insights.quote: It’s not going to be easy to reverse the $4bn sunk cost of Trump’s war on offshore wind.
insights.locator: It’s not going to be easy

insights.claim: Rusbridger lists rollbacks across climate regulation, carbon emissions, oil, gas and methane controls, EV incentives, PFAs in drinking water, wetlands, forestry, extraction leases and endangered species, saying there is no quick fix for the environment.

themes.theme: Rebuilding international, health and media institutions

insights.claim: Trump withdrew the US from more than 60 international bodies; rejoining the WHO, Paris Agreement and UN Human Rights Council is relatively easy, but rebuilding USAID after the Musk cuts will take years.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: US re-engagement with multilateral bodies is a 2029 scenario; allies will hedge until commitments are funded and durable.
insights.quote: There are more than 60 bodies in all that Trump turned his back on.

insights.claim: Restoring allied confidence requires funded commitments, consistent policy, professional diplomacy and agreements credible beyond the next election, not just talk.

insights.so_what: Public-health deterioration is a policy-reversal catalyst; watch vaccine makers and CDC funding.
